added_failures_note: Derived by this review from the reviewed node's own gate, run as two arms in scratch extractions under $TMPDIR: baseline_suite at the reviewed base 46572d2b8 (tests/tools/ in the base tree, 224 passed / 6 skipped / 13 deselected, EXIT=0, logs/review_base.log) and after_suite at the reviewed head 786814e41 (tests/tools/ in the head tree, 238 passed / 6 skipped / 13 deselected, EXIT=0, logs/review_head.log). Both arms ran to their summary line; the head adds exactly the 14 tests of tests/tools/test_dd_path_search_rerank.py and no test regresses, so added_failure_count is the set difference of the two failure-id sets and is 0. The reviewed run's own manifest carried no baseline_suite/after_suite pair (both absent), so the two arms were measured here rather than read from the reviewed record; the reviewed gate (25 passed, EXIT=0) and its declared negative control (2 failed, EXIT=1) both reproduce exactly against the reviewed head.

evidence_inputs: MERGE ORDER: the shared owner rerank_candidates/rerank_pool at this node's base and head has no decisions_key_present guard — node decisions-key-skip (dcf52306b) is NOT an ancestor of either 46572d2b8 or 786814e41, so §8's second decision (every Jev caller skips cleanly when OPENROUTER_API_KEY_IMAS_CODEX is absent) reaches the DD path only once both §8 nodes are merged into one tree. Not a defect of this node (it correctly reuses the owner), but the integration must carry both.
MODULE UNDER TEST: imas_codex.__file__ resolved to <scratch>/{{base,head}}/imas_codex/__init__.py in every arm; the shared .venv was used read-only (UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT, --no-sync).

findings.text: follow-on: the reviewed manifest carries no baseline_suite/after_suite arm pair, so the required added-failure figure cannot be read from its own record; this review measured the arms (base 224 passed, head 238 passed, both EXIT=0) and the count is 0. The change itself adds 14 tests and breaks none.

follow-on: _rerank_dd_hits discards the note rerank_candidates returns, so a search_dd_paths caller cannot tell a rerank fallback (the decisions key absent, or the 5 s budget elapsed) from a completed rerank — the two established callers surface the same note in their report (imas_codex/llm/search_tools.py:1704 and :975). The order is still never worse than embedding order; only the fallback signal is lost.

follow-on: test_read_only_server_never_reranks and ::test_dd_only_server_never_reranks assert the module switch is False rather than that rerank_candidates is never called, so the plan's never calls the rerank is pinned at the GraphSearchTool level (test_search_does_not_rerank_when_disabled) and only indirectly at the server level; the guard is falsifiable (the declared negative control reddens exactly these two).

follow_ons: The reviewed record omits baseline_suite/after_suite arms; naming them would make the record self-contained (this review measured the arms itself, added_failure_count 0).
_rerank_dd_hits drops the shared owner's fallback note; surfacing it (as imas_codex/llm/search_tools.py:1704 and :975 do) would tell a search_dd_paths caller the rerank fell back.
The two rerank failures the fragment records (electron temperature, coil current) and the intent-questionable plasma volume case are judge-quality observations for the coordinator, not node defects.
